messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: p99 latency spike observed for /v1/generate across us-west-2 after recent canary. p95 jumped from 320ms -> 1.8s, p99 -> 6.2s. Error rate (5xx) + timeouts increasing. Deploy id: rwinf-2026-03-15-02. Canary=15%.

alex-m (oncall): ack. I'm seeing the same on dashboards. Synthetic smoke tests failing: 50% timeouts. Pulling logs.

jamie-p (deploy): tagging in — I just promoted the canary to 15% at 02:08 UTC. Rolling rollout was in progress. Reverting immediately unless someone has a hotfix.

kiran-s (runtime): adding telemetry — KV cache miss rate spiked at the same timestamp, also a surge of soft evictions. Might be memory pressure from kernel change in the new image.

alex-m (oncall): timeline from traces: requests that hit model-serve instances show head latency normal, but tail stalls during kv cache refill. Example trace id: trace-0a3b.

rohit (prod-eng): suggested immediate rollback of canary to 0% and pin previous model variant. Can we execute now?

jamie-p (deploy): executing rollback. deploy-bot: rollback canary rwinf-2026-03-15-02 -> 0%

deploy-bot: Rollback initiated by jamie-p at 02:14:07 UTC. Canary traffic is being drained.

alex-m (oncall): I'm running a narrow query against metrics:
```
sum(rate(requests_count{route="/v1/generate",status=~"5.."}[1m])) by (instance)
```
Results: error_count up 7x on instances a2,a7,a9. p99 tail for a9 = 6.2s.

kiran-s (runtime): grabbing instance logs. I see repeated `KVCache::Populate` stalls and then `connection reset by peer` between the runtime and storage service. Kernel dmesg shows oom_killer logs? Not consistent though.

maria-cs: heads-up — CS is seeing user tickets about "requests timing out". Can we confirm customer impact and whether SLA page needs escalation?

alex-m (oncall): customer impact: internal SLOs show error budget burn starting. Public-facing SLA not yet breached but CS escalation likely; recommended to post status.

jamie-p (deploy): rollback complete: canary 15% -> 0% at 02:16:42 UTC. Monitoring for decay.

deploy-bot: Rollback completed. All traffic routed to stable (rwinf-stable-2026-03-01).

alex-m (oncall): metrics after rollback: p95 back to ~350ms, p99 trending down to 420ms, 5xx back to baseline. Holding watch for 10m.

kiran-s (runtime): capturing heap and KV cache stats from the problematic instances for postmortem. Saving snapshots: /var/logs/kvcache-dump/a2-6187.snap

rohit (prod-eng): action items for postmortem:
- reproduce regression with smoke harness against new image (deploy image + kernel change)
- test KV cache warming behavior under burst loads
- audit autoscaling and memory limits for model-serve pods
- roll forward plan: patch runtime to add backpressure on KV fill or increase prewarm window

maria-cs: I posted a short status update to status.redwood.ai: "We observed elevated timeouts post-deploy at 02:08 UTC affecting a subset of requests. A rollback was completed and service returned to normal. We're investigating root cause." :warning:

alex-m (oncall): handing off to kiran for deeper debug. I'll remain on-call watch for 30m and then hand to night oncall if stable.

kiran-s (runtime): taking over. Current checklist:
1) collect full logs and core dumps from a2/a7/a9
2) run smoketest harness (1000 parallel single-token calls, 95th percentile target <500ms) against canary image in staging replica set
3) replay production traffic pattern against staging with kvcache cold start

jamie-p (deploy): noted — will coordinate image rollback triggers and hold any subsequent rollouts until we sign off.

alex-m (oncall): quick note for CS: tagging customers with early errors. maria-cs, pls flag any high-priority customers.

maria-cs: flagged 3 enterprise customers (acme, beacon-health, ledgerly). CS will open dedicated threads.

kiran-s (runtime): initial hypothesis: a memory allocation change in 2026-03-15 image caused intermittent KV eviction thrashing under canary traffic. That led to tail latency as requests awaited cache fills and occasionally timed out. We'll confirm with heap snapshots.

rohit (prod-eng): if confirmed, mitigation before rollforward: tune memory limits and prewarm config or turn off the offending kernel-level optimization. Patch then smoke test.

alex-m (oncall): closing timeline notes. Root-level checklist for incident doc: detection, immediate rollback, customer notification, deeper analysis. I'll mark incident resolved for pager escalation but keep thread open for artifacts.

incident-bot: Incident recorded: INC-2026-03-15-05. Severity: Sev2. Pages: 1. Duration: 8m (02:08 -> 02:16 UTC).

jamie-p (deploy): adding link to deploy diff: https://deploys.redwood.ai/rwinf/2026-03-15/diff 

kiran-s (runtime): attaching initial dumps to the ticket: https://jira.redwood.ai/browse/INF-2891

maria-cs: CS notes saved. Will update customers with a follow-up postmortem once we have root cause.

alex-m (oncall): thanks team — great quick rollback. I'll follow up with a postmortem draft. :thumbsup:
